song.title: The Tadpole Song
song.author: Mark and Helen Johnson
song.summary: Meet Tod, the very anxious tadpole. A song-story that follows his nervous journey, and celebrates his remarkable transformation. Huge scope for harmonies, performance and choreography. Enjoy the big finale chorus, complete with full-on New Orleans jazz band. A helpful reminder for the ‘tadpole’ in us all: ‘Things’ll work out all right!’
song.teachingTips:
• Talk about the lyrics to this song. What is happening to the tadpole?
  • Can you make up some actions to help remember what happens in each verse?
  • The whole song is made up of short one-and-a-half or two-bar phrases, which makes it easy to learn. Teach the song using call-and-response and if you use Words on Screen (WOS) then take advantage of the double-click line function.
  • Choose a small group of strong singers to do the chorus harmonies. If you can, play or sing through each of the parts individually to help the singers learn their line, or even better, use the WOS which will play each harmony part for you.
  • Be prepared for, and enjoy, the backing track ‘stop’ when you sing the word ‘tadpole’.

assembly.title: Metamorphosis
assembly.description: Looking at change and understanding that there are things to be enjoyed at every stage of life.

assembly.title: It’s Challenging
assembly.description: By looking at changes in nature, this assembly helps us to explore change and how it can sometimes be difficult.

assembly.title: Feeling Good
assembly.description: This assembly explores the uniqueness of human beings and how we can help others to feel more valuable.

assembly.title: Eggs Galore!
assembly.description: This assembly explores the symbolism of eggs and their place in Pancake Day, Easter and Passover celebrations.

resources.title: Carnival Of The Animals
resources.content:
[{"key":"7571a5e97c425b07","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To listen to and identify different timbres and instrumentation
  • To create a composition that tells a story, using sound imagery
  • To perform as a group
","title":"What’s achievable","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"cad1e83f524d10bc","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Sound system; recording of Carnival of the Animals, pictures of orchestral instruments; pitched and unpitched instruments 

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"b30a0f40ea75bd22","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Many composers have been inspired to write music about animals. One of the most famous pieces is Carnival of the Animals, a suite for two pianos and orchestral instruments by Camille Saint-Saëns. Discuss the instruments of the orchestra (show some pictures) and then write the list of the movements from this piece up on the board. Play the children a few of them and see if they can guess which animal is represented each time.

What clues are given in the music? Listen out for:

  • Whether the music is loud or soft (dynamics)
  • Which instrumentation the composer has chosen to use – piano, strings, woodwind, brass, percussion? (timbre)
  • What speed is the music – is it slow or fast? (tempo)

For example:

  • The Royal March of the Lion – the music is loud, proud and stately. About halfway through the piano plays a chromatic scale in the bass (this is then echoed by the lower strings), which is the lions growling!
  • Tortoises – the music is slow and plodding with the tune in the bass (lower strings).
  • Kangaroos – The melody ‘jumps’ around the piano!
  • The Swan – The gentle broken chords in the piano depict the rippling water with the cello representing the swan gliding serenely through it. 
","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"ad19ba18537280a4","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Compose some short animal pieces. In small groups, choose an animal and discuss its characteristics. Will the music be loud or soft, fast or slow, low- or high-pitched, and which instruments will best represent the animal? Use pitched and unpitched percussion, keyboards, or any instruments that you are able to play. Then, encourage the children to imagine they are telling a story in order to give the music a structure. What is happening to the animal? Are they asleep, on the prowl, playing? What will their music need to do to show this? Ask each group to announce their animal to the class before they perform their piece. 

","title":"Step It Up!","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1873-1614695091mFFrP.png"}},{"key":"684906de51a5df1f","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

If space allows, can the children move around to the music in the style of the animals? 

","title":"Branch Out","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1874-1614695090s5QJx.png"}},{"key":"b43f3db499ed0c07","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3HgpYA5M07w","title":"The Royal March of the Lion ","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"d7e07a20da397753","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fR84Ayzcb9s","title":"Tortoises","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"5c88c22693e5923e","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8gjNhJ7l7Mk","title":"Kangaroos","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"cb324f8263e32779","layout":"video","attributes":{"url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=10Z1eNq21yc","title":"The Swan","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]
resources.summary: Listen to how Saint-Saëns uses sound imagery to depict the animals in his composition Carnival of the Animals, then, in groups, compose some musical animal stories.

resources.title: Monet's Water Lilies
resources.content:
[{"key":"31a97ba99fdb8286","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Monet (1840-1926) made a series of 250 paintings depicting the water lilies in his garden throughout the different seasons; in these he responded to the changing colours, textures and light in the garden. 

Is there a school pond that the children could study? If so, get them to create drawings and paintings, responding to it on different days throughout the seasons. (Or use another area of the school such as a garden or perhaps a tree.) How does it look in spring? Are there new colours and shapes? 

Have an exhibition to celebrate all the different ways they individually perceive and respond to this scene.

","title":"","background_color":""}}]

resources.title: Create A Sparkyard Song Trail!
resources.content:
[{"key":"85ab99323ddf270a","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/SYHomepageImages/LandscapeImages/sy-song-trail-updated-no-neg-1750855970WlYvf.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"7b00ffa0c50109ef","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Raise the profile of singing and develop a love of songs by organising a ‘Sparkyard song trail’ around the school grounds. It’s a great way to celebrate and encourage singing in every corner of your school!

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"60f5e4c5b2df2d2a","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

  1. Bluetooth speakers

  2. A device (e.g. iPad, tablet or phone)

  3. Trail maps (optional)

  4. QR code labels (instructions below)

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"6c22faa70fd70019","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"1. Choose Your Songs","background_color":"#65A22F"}},{"key":"c63077077d2e6998","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

First, choose your Sparkyard songs and rhymes. The number you choose will depend on how long you would like your trail to be, but we recommend about eight songs. You could choose songs that are completely new or opt for ones the children have been working on.

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"d4797fa622bfd224","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"2. Choose your locations","background_color":"#F27021"}},{"key":"23b7d2c26b9aacc5","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Next, think about where you like each song to be sung. Some songs may lend themselves to a particular location in the school – e.g. Lunchtime Queue outside the dinner hall; Let’s Be Quiet in the quiet area; Mr Oak Tree by an oak tree or The Tadpole Song by the school pond. If your trail passes classrooms, why not choose songs that are favourites of a particular teacher? This is a lovely way for the children to understand that singing is valued by each staff member.  

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"d61c9b8e2950fe24","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/BlogGuideImages/singing-trail-1750938568a75xr.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"2cc8af4e934958dd","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"3. Generate QR Codes","background_color":"#DE2862"}},{"key":"e729d70e3b825c51","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Next, generate a QR code for each song.

  • Choose the song you want to share. 
  • Find the three little dots icon on the play bar and on the song page.  
  • Click ‘Share’ and then ‘Generate Share Link.’

Sparkyard will give you a QR code that you can download or screengrab, and it can then be printed to create a simple poster/label and placed at the appropriate location.

(Don't forget that Share Links last for 14 days, but can be renewed in your Manage Account area.)

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"3bde0b1e5a1c3d9c","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"4. Test out your route! ","background_color":"#8DC261"}},{"key":"067d91fc62fb8682","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Walk around the grounds with your device and check that the QR code works in each location. Don’t forget to pack your Bluetooth speakers!

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"ada9af72ec0050e2","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"5. Explore the song trail!","background_color":"#3982BA"}},{"key":"3f14716f8cc8952e","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

At each location, scan the QR code to access the song. Enjoy singing the song and talk about it. Can the children say why it suits the location?

If you are doing this activity in small groups, you might like to provide a map or create some simple clues to identify each location.

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"51735c127a55e400","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/BlogGuideImages/song-trail-2-1750938497V0tbT.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"0f574d08b5f509aa","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"6. Back in the Classroom","background_color":"#15A881"}},{"key":"c6c4c673523a3a84","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Once the trail is complete, head back to the classroom. Can the children create their own simple map of their journey around the school and write down the song they sang in each location. Which was their favourite? Which songs would they like to sing again?

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"d7c441ca9e3c2585","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"7. Follow Up","background_color":"#E15B64"}},{"key":"fe47f225f5386b49","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

As a follow-up, why not encourage the children to create their own song trails. Which songs would they choose and where might they sing them? They could think about locations in the school or in their local environment.

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"5548ab1ca644c528","layout":"title-block","attributes":{"title":"Some further ideas","background_color":"#F5BB26"}},{"key":"ebd7fca71a072128","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"
  • Perhaps link the songs to a particular curriculum area (e.g. history) – a great ‘hook’ at the start of a new topic or sequence of learning.  
  • Create a Sparkyard song trail as part of a school event (e.g. a school fête) – a great way to involve families and get everyone singing.
  • Set up a trail as part of an Arts Week or to celebrate a special time in the school calendar (e.g. World Book Day; National Poetry Day; Children’s Mental Health Week; Easter).
  • Check out our Extreme Singing blog and hold a competition to see who can find the most exciting place to sing!
","title":"","noMargin":false}}]
